context:
Port the row-count guard already proven on three sibling engine builders to
the fourth (w1), decide the cheapest correct per-query vacuity check for
TPC-Havoc's specific query set (w2, deciding between a full classification map
and a simpler "TPC-H canonical is never legitimately empty" assertion), align
the shared _report's stale-baseline behavior with the cross-surface gate's
precedent (w3), and lock all three in with negative tests (w4).
description:
SOUNDNESS-CRITICAL COMPARATOR SURFACE: this TODO's work is in
benchbox/core/tpchavoc/equivalence.py, the blocking TPC-Havoc SQL equivalence
gate. It is adjacent to, and shares helpers with, benchbox/core/tpchavoc/validation.py
(covered by .github/CODEOWNERS as `benchbox/core/**/validation.py @joeharris76`)
and mirrors the discipline of benchbox/core/equivalence/cross_surface.py
(covered as `benchbox/core/equivalence/** @joeharris76`). Even though
`benchbox/core/tpchavoc/equivalence.py` itself is not literally matched by
either existing CODEOWNERS glob (verified: only `core/**/validation.py` and
`core/equivalence/**` are listed in .github/CODEOWNERS as of this writing),
it IS the hard, blocking correctness gate for TPC-Havoc and must be treated as
soundness-critical - request code-owner review on the PR explicitly rather
than relying on the glob to force it, and flag in the PR description that
CODEOWNERS coverage for this file may itself be worth extending.

Verified by reading benchbox/core/tpchavoc/equivalence.py on this branch:

- `build_postgres_with_tpch` (lines 370-431) verifies every TPC-H table loaded
  >0 rows before sampling (lines 412-419: `table_stats.get(table, 0) <= 0`
  raises `RuntimeError`), with the comment "A silent empty/partial load would
  make every variant compare empty-vs-empty and report a FALSE green."
- `build_datafusion_with_tpch` (lines 588-618) has the identical guard (lines
  611-614).
- `build_clickhouse_with_tpch` (lines 770-808) has the identical guard (lines
  800-803).
- `build_duckdb_with_tpch` (lines 296-316), the BLOCKING gate builder that
  every other engine's builder was modeled after, has NO such guard: it calls
  `DuckDBAdapter(database=":memory:").load_data(tpchavoc, connection, data_dir)`
  and returns immediately, never checking the load actually populated rows.
  A silent partial/empty DuckDB load would make `find_divergences` compare
  empty-vs-empty for every affected query and the hard gate would report a
  FALSE green - the exact failure mode the three sibling engines were
  explicitly hardened against.
- `find_divergences` (lines 198-274) has no per-query vacuity check: it never
  inspects whether `original` (the canonical query's row count) is empty
  before comparing to each variant. Compare this to
  `benchbox/core/equivalence/cross_surface.py`'s `legitimately_empty` /
  vacuous-cell handling (`CrossSurfaceGate.legitimately_empty`,
  cross_surface.py:372-382, and the FAILURE line at cross_surface.py:1183-1187
  `GATE FAILURE - vacuous empty-vs-empty queries ... not classified`), which
  fails the gate on any unclassified 0-row reference rather than silently
  passing an empty-vs-empty comparison.
- `_report` (lines 434-470), shared by every TPC-Havoc engine, returns
  `1 if new else 0` (line 470) - it does NOT fail when `resolved` (a
  previously-known divergence that no longer reproduces) is non-empty; it
  only PRINTS a message to update the baseline (line 466-467). Compare this
  to the cross-surface gate's own `_report`
  (benchbox/core/equivalence/cross_surface.py:1188-1196), which explicitly
  fails on `resolved`: "GATE FAILURE - previously-known divergences now
  equivalent ... remove the stale baseline entry in a reviewed change" and
  `return 1 if (new or resolved or missing_backends or unclassified_empty) else 0`.
  So today a stale TPC-Havoc `KNOWN_DIVERGENCES`/`POSTGRES_KNOWN_DIVERGENCES`/
  etc. entry (whose divergence has since been fixed) can sit indefinitely
  without forcing anyone to prune it, unlike the cross-surface gate's
  behavior.

anti_patterns.dont: change _report's stale-baseline behavior (w3) without first running all four report modes and confirming which currently-declared entries would newly fail
anti_patterns.why: a surprise CI break in a non-blocking sample job is still a broken PR.

anti_patterns.dont: fork find_divergences per engine to add the vacuity check
anti_patterns.why: it is already engine-agnostic (takes connection/canonical_query/translate_variant as parameters); extend it in place.

anti_patterns.dont: silently classify an unexpected empty canonical query as 'legitimately empty' to make w2's implementation easier
anti_patterns.why: that is exactly the coverage-theater w4 of cross-surface-oracle-remediation fixed for SSB; investigate and either fix the root cause or classify with a real, written rationale.

anti_patterns.dont: special-case DuckDB's row-count check differently in shape from the Postgres/DataFusion/ClickHouse guards
anti_patterns.why: a fifth engine author should be able to copy any one of the four verbatim.

deferrals.reason: Out of scope; a future engine sample should copy the hardened build_duckdb_with_tpch/find_divergences/_report from this TODO, not require a repeat audit.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] conditional-unmet: Guidance for a hypothetical future fifth TPC-Havoc engine sample; not actionable until such an engine sample exists.
deferrals.summary: Apply the same vacuity/staleness hardening pattern to any future fifth TPC-Havoc engine sample.

preserves.behavior: The DuckDB SQL equivalence gate stays the hard, blocking gate; `make tpchavoc-equivalence-report` reports `checked 220 variants - 0 divergent, 220 equivalent` (or the then-current true count) with exit 0 on a healthy tree, unchanged by this hardening.

The Postgres/DataFusion/ClickHouse samples (`make tpchavoc-equivalence-report-postgres/-datafusion/-clickhouse`) stay green; the shared `_report` change in w3 must not newly fail them on entries that are still live.
find_divergences, validate_variant_equivalence, and _report remain shared/engine-agnostic - no per-engine fork introduced by this hardening.

prior_art.concept: benchbox/core/equivalence/cross_surface.py:372-382 CrossSurfaceGate.legitimately_empty and cross_surface.py:1183-1196 _report's vacuous/stale handling - the reference pattern for per-query vacuity classification and stale-baseline failure; port the DESIGN (explicit classification + fail-on-stale), do not fork the cross-surface code itself since TPC-Havoc's Divergence/known-divergence shapes differ (per-variant vs per-backend-cell).

benchbox/core/tpchavoc/equivalence.py:198-274 find_divergences - the shared, engine-agnostic comparator loop; add the per-query empty check here so all four engines (DuckDB, Postgres, DataFusion, ClickHouse) benefit, not just DuckDB.

benchbox/core/tpchavoc/equivalence.py:412-419 (build_postgres_with_tpch), 611-614 (build_datafusion_with_tpch), 800-803 (build_clickhouse_with_tpch) - the three existing row-count guard implementations to mirror for build_duckdb_with_tpch.

benchbox/core/tpchavoc/equivalence.py:434-470 _report - shared by every engine; the resolved-fails-the-gate change here also affects Postgres/DataFusion/ClickHouse samples, which is intentional (their baselines should not rot either) but must be verified non-disruptive to those non-blocking samples.

work_units.notes:
Implemented exactly as scoped. Verified DuckDBAdapter.load_data already
returns `(table_stats, loading_time, None)` - the same 3-tuple shape the
Postgres/DataFusion/ClickHouse builders destructure via
`table_stats, _, _ = adapter.load_data(...)` - so no adapter contract
change was needed. build_duckdb_with_tpch now wraps schema creation + load
in try/except, raises `RuntimeError("DuckDB TPC-H load failed - no rows in
{empty} (stats={table_stats})")` on any 0-row table (identical message
shape to the three siblings), and closes the connection before re-raising
so a failed build never leaks a DuckDB handle. Verified live: 220 variants
still checked, 0 divergent after the change (make tpchavoc-equivalence-report).
work_units.summary: Add a row-count guard to build_duckdb_with_tpch mirroring the Postgres/DataFusion/ClickHouse builders

work_units.notes:
Chose option (b), the simpler blanket assertion, per the open_questions
default: live DuckDB/DataFusion/ClickHouse runs (w1/w3 verification) and
the module's own docstring precedent (EQUIVALENCE_SCALE=0.1 was originally
chosen specifically so no gated query is vacuous - Q17 was the known
SF=0.01 vacuity case) both confirm no TPC-H canonical query is empty at
EQUIVALENCE_SCALE today, so no genuine legitimately-empty case exists to
justify a classification map. Implemented directly in `find_divergences`
(not per-caller) per the prior_art guidance ("add the per-query empty
check here so all four engines benefit") and the anti_pattern against
forking the comparator per engine: when the canonical query returns 0
rows, one `Divergence(query_id, 0, "...vacuous...")` is appended and the
variant loop for that query is skipped entirely (mirrors the existing
canonical-failure `except`+`continue` shape immediately above it) - no
variant of a vacuous-canonical query is ever silently marked equivalent.
No classification map was added since no legitimately-empty query exists
to require one; if one is ever found, promote to the dict[int, str]
shape described in option (a) at that point (documented in the
function's new docstring paragraph).
work_units.summary: Add a per-query empty-vs-empty detection to find_divergences (or its callers), require explicit classification

work_units.notes:
Changed `_report`'s return statement to `return 1 if (new or resolved)
else 0` and upgraded the resolved-baseline print to a "GATE FAILURE -
..." line (matching cross_surface.py's message class/wording, though the
two `_report`s remain separate functions per the anti_patterns - no
shared helper introduced). Verified live, post-change, all four report
modes: DuckDB hard gate (KNOWN_DIVERGENCES={}) 220/220 equivalent, exit 0;
DataFusion (DATAFUSION_KNOWN_DIVERGENCES={}) 206/206 equivalent, exit 0;
ClickHouse (CLICKHOUSE_KNOWN_DIVERGENCES has 7 live entries) - all 7 still
reproduce (none resolved), 195/202 equivalent, exit 0; Postgres could not
be run live (no reachable Postgres server in this environment - the
sample cleanly SKIPs with exit 0 on psycopg.OperationalError, unchanged by
this TODO), but POSTGRES_KNOWN_DIVERGENCES is the empty dict `{}`, so
`resolved` is trivially empty regardless of live results - confirmed by
code inspection, not just the skip path.
work_units.summary: Make _report fail (not just print) on a stale/resolved known-divergence baseline, matching cross_surface.py's behavior

Added tests/unit/core/tpchavoc/test_tpchavoc_vacuity_guard.py (fast/unit,
pure fakes, no real DuckDB data generation - mirrors

  - test_find_divergences_vacuity_guard_fails_on_empty_canonical_query (w2)
  - test_find_divergences_vacuity_guard_does_not_flag_a_nonempty_canonical_query (w2 regression guard)
  - test_report_vacuity_guard_fails_on_stale_resolved_baseline (w3)
  - test_report_vacuity_guard_stays_green_with_no_new_or_resolved_entries (w3 regression guard)
All 5 pass under `pytest tests/unit/core/tpchavoc/ -k vacuity -v`, and the
full tests/unit/core/tpchavoc/ suite (78 tests) stays green.
work_units.summary: Add negative tests for each of w1-w3 (vacuous load, vacuous query, stale baseline all fail the gate)
